newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Feb spot natgas notionally lower on weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Feb spot natgas notionally lower on weather.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices for February swing delivery were notionally lower again on Friday, pressured by forecasts calling for milder weather next week throughout most of the U.S., sources said.
February swing prices on the Gulf Coast pipes drifted nearly 10 cents lower into the low-to-mid $2.70s as warmer temperatures moved into the southern plains and stretched into parts of the Midwest.
Revised forecasts are now calling for mostly above-normal temperatures in the Mid-Atlantic states through at least the middle of next week.
As a result of the warmer-than-expected forecasts in the East, prices fell another five cents today at the New York city-gate to about $3.45.
Similarly on the Appalachian pipes prices were down at least five cents to about $3 per mmBtu.
In the Midcontinent, February prices were notionally more than 20 cents lower in the $2.47-2.52 range, with Demarcation quoted around $2.55.
Chicago city-gate values were talked in the mid-$3.20s.
In West Texas, where temperatures are expected to reach 10-15 degrees above normal by Sunday, Permian prices softened by about 15 cents to the $2.34-2.39 range.
Swing prices at the southern California border were talked nearly 10 cents lower in the low-$2.50s.
